channel.title: AI on 梦兽编程
channel.description: Recent content in AI on 梦兽编程

item.title: Who Draws the Kill Line for AI Models? Stop Letting Benchmarks Replace Engineering Reality
item.description: From prompt caching and thinking tokens to long context and inference infrastructure, a practical look at the real cost and engineering strength of Chinese foundation models.

item.title: AI Tool Calling: Why Rust Isn't the Best Choice
item.description: After reading a 2026 Medium hit, I rebuilt the same weather CLI in five languages and re-evaluated Rust, Go, Zig, Bun, and Node.js for AI tool calling / function calling.

item.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 Released: 1M Context, Official Price Hike Warning
item.description: DeepSeek released deepseek-v4-pro (0813) on 2026-08-13: 1M context, 384K max output, $0.435/M input and $0.87/M output, with cache-hit input at just $0.003625/M. The official docs also warn that overall API pricing will rise significantly in the near future. Includes Claude Code / Codex setup and community benchmark roundup.

item.title: Companies Offer 30K for Agent Engineers, Demo Writers Can't Get Hired
item.description: Companies can't hire production-ready agent engineers at 30K a month while demo writers can't find jobs. We break the gap into four skill blocks, each backed by real production cases from Anthropic, Cognition, and AWS, plus three runnable code examples

item.title: Stop Teaching AI to Code Step by Step: The Claude Code Team's #1 Advice Is 'Give It Back Its Judgment'
item.description: The counterintuitive advice from the Claude Code team at AIE 2026: don't tell Fable when to write tests — let it decide for itself. Likewise, let Fable decide which tasks should be delegated to cheaper models. This strategy is not only cheaper, but more effective.

item.title: Newer Claude Models Are Worse at Using Your Tools: An Engineering Trap of RL Training Backfire
item.description: Armin discovered that Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5 are actually more error-prone than older models when calling Pi's custom editing tool — because RL training overfits them to Claude Code's built-in tools. This is a wake-up call for every third-party coding harness.

item.title: After AI Codes 10x Faster Than You, the Only Skill That Holds Value Is 'Understanding'
item.description: When AI can rewrite a JavaScript runtime in days, 'being able to write code' is no longer a moat. Geoffrey Litt proposes 'understand to participate,' pointing directly at the core paradox of AI programming: the faster the code is written, the shallower the understanding, and the heavier the cognitive debt.

item.title: SOTA on Paper, Engineering Traps in Production: Claude Opus 5's Hidden Risks
item.description: Claude Opus 5 tops Frontier-Bench and CursorBench at half the price of Fable 5. We look past the benchmarks to three engineering traps most teams miss.

item.title: llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang: Three Inference Engines, Three Completely Different Paths
item.description: llama.cpp, vLLM, and SGLang aren't competitors in the same lane — they're built on entirely different design assumptions. Which one fits your workload? The answer depends on one metric you probably haven't measured.

item.title: BigQuery AI.AGG: When GROUP BY Starts Calling Gemini
item.description: Google wired Gemini into a BigQuery aggregate. Each group now returns one natural-language answer. We walk through SQL semantics, hidden batching, cost pitfalls, and four engineering guardrails.

item.title: Seven Questions About Kimi K3: China's Quiet Fable 5 Contender
item.description: Moonshot AI teased K3 with a 36-second video, but the real story was already unfolding on Chatbot Arena — where an anonymous model codenamed Kivine has been building 3D pages, cloning video effects, and going toe-to-toe with Claude Fable 5. Here's what actually matters.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 3): Refactoring Tools into a Skill Registry with Traits
item.description: Part 3 replaces the Part 1 match dispatcher with a Rust trait system: Skill, Registry, DynSkill, schemars-generated JSON Schema, parallel calls, error classification, retries, hooks, and permission gates.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 4): State Machines for Multi-Step Tasks
item.description: Part 4 introduces state machines for multi-step tasks: Node trait, Graph runner, SQLite checkpointing, Interrupt suspend/resume, PermissionMode gates, and NodeHook cross-cutting logic.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 5): Multi-Agent Crews
item.description: Part 5 covers multi-agent collaboration: when to add agents and when not to. The Agent trait, Crew parallel/sequential dispatch, Router, debate protocol, and composing with Part 3's skill registry and Part 4's state machine.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust — Part 2: Structured Prompt Architecture and the Cache Boundary
item.description: Following Part 1's tool-calling loop, Part 2 dives into Agent system prompt architecture: Identity, Instructions, Output, Examples, and Context layers, plus Anthropic Prompt Caching and prompt fingerprinting for regression testing.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust — The Tool-Calling Loop Explained
item.description: A deep dive into the core mechanism of AI agents: the tool-calling loop. Through a ~200-line Rust implementation, we break down how models gain the ability to act via tool use, and why the architecture behind Claude Code and GitHub Copilot is the same fundamental loop.

item.title: Stop Getting Interrupted by Claude Code. Run It Inside a Container and Let It Go Wild.
item.description: The most annoying thing about Claude Code is getting interrupted by permission prompts every few seconds. Code Container solves this with Docker: 300ms startup, full isolation, let it rm -rf all it wants. Here's how it works and how to use it.

item.title: Codex Mobile with Third-Party API: Exploiting the Auth/Model Layer Decoupling
item.description: Got Codex Mobile working with a third-party API relay. The key insight: Auth and Model layers are fully decoupled — ChatGPT handles identity, coding.rexai.top handles inference. Full configuration guide included.

item.title: Ralph Loop and Codex /goal: Why Agents Can Keep Working for Hours
item.description: What keeps coding agents running on long tasks isn't stronger models — it's goal state management and auto-continuation. A breakdown of Ralph Loop and Codex /goal, two engineering approaches to the same problem.

item.title: Sub-Agents vs Agent Teams: The Architecture Decision That Can Wreck Your System
item.description: The real question is how to choose between Sub-Agents and Agent Teams. Most people immediately think of multi-agent systems when tasks get complex, but that's often the wrong starting point. Understanding the answer can save you countless hours of rework.

item.title: Did Claude Opus 4.7 Secretly Raise Prices? 497 Developers Reveal the Truth
item.description: 497 anonymous developer submissions reveal Claude Opus 4.7 consumes 37.3% more tokens than 4.6 on average, with API costs rising proportionally. Here's what caused the 'hidden price hike' and what you can do about it.

item.title: The Claude Code Leak: How an Accident Sparked a Rust Rewrite Wave
item.description: In March 2026, Claude Code's 500k+ lines of TypeScript source code were accidentally leaked. Instead of panic, the developer community responded by rewriting the entire project in Rust. How did this mess turn into Rust's best advertisement for AI infrastructure?

item.title: Your AI Agent Can Think, But It Can't Remember
item.description: AI agents can reason, plan, and converse—but forget everything once the session ends. The Ghost project solves this with a pure PostgreSQL-based infrastructure, turning the database into the agent's memory palace.

item.title: Cramming a 400B Model into 48GB: The Magic Behind LLM in a Flash
item.description: An Apple paper from 2023 made it possible to run a 400 billion parameter model on an ordinary MacBook. The core technologies—MoE and quantization—hide an engineering philosophy built around on-demand loading.

item.title: 90 Seconds of Waiting, Gone: How oMLX Buries Ollama on Mac
item.description: oMLX is built for Apple Silicon, using the MLX framework, SSD-backed KV cache, and continuous batching to cut TTFT from 90 seconds to 1-3 seconds in long-context scenarios, comprehensively outperforming Ollama.

item.title: Claude Code Channels: Give Your AI Coding Assistant a Phone Number
item.description: A hands-on look at Claude Code Channels, letting you control your AI coding assistant through Telegram, Discord, and more — no matter where you are.

item.title: Don't Build a Thousand Agents: How Ramp Automates Finance with One Agent
item.description: Ramp, America's fastest-growing enterprise finance platform valued at $32B with 50,000+ customers and $100B+ in annual transaction volume, chose a 'one Agent + a thousand skills' architecture over building many agents. This is a deep dive into Ramp's AI实战经验.

item.title: Mistral Forge Deep Dive: The Nuclear Weapon for Enterprise Fine-tuning
item.description: Spent 3 hours reading the official documentation. Forge wants to turn fine-tuning into an all-in-one service - you just feed it data, and it handles everything else. But how low is the barrier really?

item.title: AI Programming Hits the 'Review Bottleneck'? Mistral Drops an Open-Source Bomb
item.description: Mistral AI releases Leanstral, the first open-source Lean 4 code agent that lets AI both write code and prove its correctness. Let's talk about formal verification and AI programming.

item.title: AI Agents Finally Make Literate Programming Worth Trying
item.description: Literate programming has been around for 40 years but never caught on — because maintaining parallel narratives of code and prose is exhausting. AI agents change that equation entirely.

item.title: You Use AI for Coding, But Have You Ever Used One That Holds Grudges?
item.description: When AI programming tools become goldfish - discussing the context loss pain point and how to make AI remember what you're working on

item.title: Locking Down Your Local AI Agent: An Agent Safehouse Review
item.description: A macOS tool that sandboxes AI agents like Claude Code and Codex, preventing accidental file deletions and credential leaks once and for all.

item.title: OpenClaw Multi-Bot Team Collaboration: Three Architecture Patterns Compared
item.description: Build multiple independent Telegram Bots into a collaborative Agent team. This article covers three architecture patterns and complete configuration methods.

item.title: Karpathy's Latest Work: Complete GPT in 200 Lines of Code - The Most Adorable AI Tutorial
item.description: Andrej Karpathy has done it again! This time he implemented a trainable, inferable GPT model in just 200 lines of pure Python with no dependencies. This might be the most concise large language model implementation ever.

item.title: Neural Network Reverse Engineering: When Machine Learning Becomes a Puzzle Game
item.description: Jane Street released a special ML puzzle: given the complete neural network weights, find an input that makes it output non-zero. This isn't a typical black-box attack - it requires truly understanding what the network is computing. A college student spent days, going from linear programming to SAT solvers, and finally discovered the network was hiding an MD5 hash function.

item.title: Agno-Go: Building AI Agents in Go - What's it Like Being 16x Faster than Python?
item.description: Rewriting AI Agent framework in Go brings 16x performance boost, 180ns agent startup, and only 1.2KB memory footprint - this is the extreme experience Agno-Go delivers

item.title: CPU-GPU Overlap Inference Starter Guide: Cut 30% Wait Time with Python
item.description: Clarify the CPU/GPU split in PyTorch inference and walk through overlapping techniques that slash latency.
